data.name: Hamdiya
data.gender_notes: Hamdiya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Hamdiya means ‘she who praises or admires’. This name is derived from the root hmd, which carries the meaning of ‘to praise, to admire, to give thanks, to glorify, and to extol’. In Islamic history, Hamdiya is the name of a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who was known for her deep faith and piety. The name Hamdiya carries the meaning “Praiser, Admirer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hamdiya usually hope their child will grow to embody praiser, admirer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Hamdiya belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Praiser, Admirer.”

in_arabic.name: حمدية
in_arabic.meaning: معنى: السعادة والرضا والثناء والشكر والحمد
in_arabic.long_meaning: حمدية: اسم علم للإناث، مشتق من الحمد، الذي هو شكر الله تعالى على كل خير. يُعتبر الحمد من أركان الإسلام، ويكون في صلاة الفجر، وفي كل صلاة، ويُشكر الله تعالى على نعمة النوم، واليقظة، والرزق. ويُعتبر الحمد من أهم العلامات على حب الله تعالى لعباده، ويُظهر حبهم لله تعالى. ويُستخدم الحمد في القرآن الكريم في العديد من الآيات، مثل: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَخَذَ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَى النَّفَرِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَا تَرَكَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ دَيَّتًا) (الأنبياء: 105). وبالتالي، يُعتبر الحمد اسمًا علمًا ممتازًا، يُشير إلى العلاقة بين الإنسان وربه، ويُظهر حب الله تعالى للبشرية.

in_english.name: Hamdiya
in_english.meaning: Meaning: Happiness, satisfaction, praise, gratitude, and thanksgiving
in_english.long_meaning: Hamdiya: A female Arabic name, derived from the word 'hamd', which is gratitude to Allah for all the good things. Hamd is considered one of the pillars of Islam, and is recited in the morning prayer and in every prayer, thanking Allah for the blessings of sleep and wakefulness, and for the provision of food. Hamd is used in the Quran in many verses, such as: (And if your Lord had willed, He could have taken away their offspring, and He has power to do all that He wills) (Al-Anbiya: 105). Therefore, Hamdya is a notable name that indicates the relationship between man and his Lord, and shows the love of Allah for humanity.
